title: SSO/SAML session policy: define re-auth, JIT provisioning mapping, logout propagation
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Current SSO/SAML behavior is inconsistent across hosted private deployments: JIT provisioning creates accounts without clear session lifecycle, MFA expectations are not enforced consistently for admin flows, and logout/SLO signals are not reliably propagated to active sessions. We need a unified session management policy that covers: 1) JIT-provisioned users and attribute mapping for RBAC v2, 2) MFA expectations and re-auth triggers for sensitive routes, 3) session lifetimes (idle/absolute), 4) SP-initiated and IdP-initiated logout propagation, and 5) admin controls for forced user sign-out and session revocation.
decision: Adopt a single canonical session policy across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments: idle timeout = 30m, absolute max session lifetime = 12h, refresh tokens scoped to device and rotated every 6h, require re-auth (IdP redirect) for admin/billing routes if last authentication > 1h OR if account created by JIT within last 10m, treat IdP-initiated SLO as authoritative and immediately mark all server-side sessions revoked. JIT provisioning will map SAML groups to RBAC v2 roles using attribute 'redwood_groups' and will create accounts in disabled state until first successful IdP-auth; on first sign-in, evaluate MFA policy and require it when role requires elevated access.
acceptance_criteria: Documented session lifecycle and mapping in Confluence and in API docs
SSO-initiated logout (SLO) triggers immediate server-side session revocation and audit event
Re-auth enforced for /console/admin and /billing when last auth > 1h
JIT-provisioned users receive role mapping via redwood_groups and are prompted for MFA on first session when required
Automated tests for SLO propagation and session revocation in CI pipeline
Rollout plan with feature flag and telemetry to monitor session churn and reauth rates
comments: 2026-02-25 Maya Patel: Kickoff — compiling incidents where IdP SLO didn't clear sessions (INC-2025, INC-2041). Captured sample SAML assertions from Okta and Azure.

2026-02-27 Luca Hernandez: Spike complete — IdP SLO currently handled only by front-end cookie purge; backend session store (redis) not notified. Need a message bus event or synchronous endpoint from SSO middleware.
2026-03-01 Priya Singh (Product): PM priority is high — compliance customers require proof of session termination within 5s of IdP logout. Consider exposing admin endpoint for bulk revoke.

2026-03-03 Security review notes from Omar Khalid: MFA policy must be measurable — require step-up for any admin API that modifies RBAC roles. Also flagged SCIM deprovision propagation as separate item (SEC-412).

2026-03-04 Design feedback (Ava Chen): UX for re-auth should surface reason — 'Re-auth required for admin access' and not redirect to IdP repeatedly if user cancels. Suggest fallback to ephemeral session with very short TTL.

2026-03-05 Luca Hernandez: Implementation plan submitted in PR #2148 — adds backend SLO webhook endpoint, session revocation worker, and session metadata to track last_auth_ts and auth_method. Tests pending.
next_steps: Merge backend SLO webhook PR and add feature flag (ENG-8793-flag)
Add integration test that simulates IdP SLO and asserts server-side session revocation within 5s
Add UI flows for re-auth UX and add telemetry for reauth prompts and outcomes
Coordinate roll-forward with Dedicated and Private ops to ensure SLO endpoint is reachable from customer IdPs
Schedule security review session with Omar and compliance for customer-facing statement
notes: Edge cases: offline IdP (can't reach SLO endpoint) — fallback to marking sessions 'pending_revoke' and revoke on next refresh; JIT accounts created by SCIM vs SAML should have unified lifecycle; need to audit long-lived API keys vs interactive sessions. Consider future extension: bind sessions to device fingerprint and IP for higher assurance.
risk_assessment: Medium-High: Incorrect handling may cause false positives (unexpected logouts) or false negatives (stale active sessions). Must include telemetry and quick rollback via feature flag.
implementation_breakdown: Backend: SLO webhook endpoint + session revocation worker (Luca)
Auth: enrich session token with last_auth_ts and auth_method, enforce reauth on guarded routes (Auth team)
JIT provisioning: map redwood_groups to RBAC v2 roles and mark account pending_mfa if required (Onboarding team)
Frontend: re-auth UX and admin forced-logout control (Design + Web)
Ops: expose SLO endpoint in Private/VPC deployment docs and health checks (Platform)
estimated_impact_metrics: % of sessions revoked within 5s of SLO target >= 95%
Reauth conversion rate for admin flows (target >= 90% success)
Reduction in stale sessions older than 12h by 99%
owner_notes: Keep rollout conservative: enable for 10% of orgs first, watch telemetry for unexpected logout spikes, then 50% before global. Coordinate communication with Customer Success for enterprise tenants.
completion_criteria: All acceptance criteria met, security review signed off, PRs merged, feature flag toggles in place, and runbook updated for SLO troubleshooting.
